public_existing_mechanisms.mechanical_fact: Idempotency-Key is intended to make non-idempotent methods fault-tolerant; a key must be unique and not reused for a different payload.
Same idempotency key can replay a prior request result under documented scope, illustrating provider-side recovery semantics rather than blind client retry.

provider_modes.reconcilable: stable eval_id plus durable query-by-ID reconciliation; provider effects are unique by semantic eval identity in this local reference
provider_modes.neither: no idempotent replay guarantee and no reconciliation API; unresolved durable intent must become UNKNOWN on restart without POST replay

precommitted_cases: prewire crash after durable intent / reconcilable -> reconcile miss then exactly one execute/effect and COMPLETE
prewire crash after durable intent / neither -> BLOCKED_UNKNOWN with zero execute/effect
controller SIGKILL after provider durable effect commit but before response read / reconcilable -> reconcile existing effect, no second execute, COMPLETE
controller SIGKILL after provider durable effect commit but before response read / neither -> BLOCKED_UNKNOWN, no second execute
provider process crash after durable effect commit but before response send / reconcilable -> restart provider then reconcile effect, no second execute, COMPLETE
provider process crash after durable effect commit but before response send / neither -> BLOCKED_UNKNOWN, no second execute
terminal_gate: After terminal COMPLETE or BLOCKED_UNKNOWN, a second fresh controller resume must cause zero additional provider execute or reconcile calls.
all_pass_rule: Every case must satisfy its exact effect/call/outcome/terminal gate; otherwise report FAIL without modifying the mechanism.
scope: Loopback HTTP, separate provider/controller OS processes, SQLite FULL/WAL durability. Does not prove arbitrary remote provider semantics or network partitions outside tested boundaries.
ordered_protocol: checkpoint exact scope and preserve nonempty frontier
